subject: Re: KMS options & encryption requirements — post-call recap

Subject: KMS options & encryption requirements — post-call recap

Hi Tim — thanks for taking time earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

Summary of ask:
- Acme needs to ensure PII is protected in-transit and at-rest, with an option for customer-managed keys (HSM-backed KMS).
- Data retention & logging controls: specific retention windows for PII/audit logs and separation of sensitive telemetry.
- SOC 2 evidence and diagrams showing key flows and access boundaries.

What Redwood can provide (high-level):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 supported and recommended).
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption for model artifacts and data stores.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): BYOK via standard KMS integrations; HSM-backed key storage supported for private deployments / Dedicated.
- Operational controls: audit logs, role-based access controls, and optional log partitioning per tenant.

Open questions for you (so we can scope the SOW):
1) Which classes of PII do you consider regulated (e.g., PHI vs. contact info)?
2) Required retention periods for PII, audit logs, and backups (default Redwood retention is 90 days for logs).
3) Is it a requirement that Redwood never sees plaintext (i.e., must we support client-side encryption)?

Attachments: redwood-kms-options.pdf (high-level options + pricing impact)

Next suggested steps:
- Vivek to run a short tech deep-dive on the key flow and logging controls (30–45 min).
- We’ll share an architecture diagram and SOC 2 evidence bundle.
- If CMK/HSM is required, we’ll prepare a bill-of-materials for Dedicated or Private deployment options.

Would you be available next week for the tech deep-dive? I can loop in Vivek and Rishi to cover security and pricing implications.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. A few specifics from our side to help scope: 

- Encryption in-transit: must support TLS 1.2 minimum; TLS 1.3 preferred.
- At-rest: AES-256 required for all backups and databases.
- Key management: our procurement/security team requires customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed storage. We need proof keys are not exportable from HSMs and support for quarterly rotation.
- Plaintext access: for regulatory reasons, we need confirmation whether Redwood will ever have access to plaintext for request/responses or intermediate caches. If guaranteed no plaintext access is not achievable, we need to scope client-side encryption options.
- Logging & retention: audit logs must be retained 7 years; PII retention policy: 5 years unless otherwise requested for deletion. Backups must respect retention windows.
- Compliance evidence: we need SOC 2 Type II report and specifics around encryption controls.

Can you provide a diagram of key flow (how keys are used in transit/at-rest, where they are stored, and whether Redwood's control plane touches plaintext)? Also include any limitations for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.

If you can send the diagrams and an initial run-rate impact for HSM-backed keys, we can move to the vendor approval queue.

—Tim
Tim Jones
Head of Security, Acme Health

Subject: Re: KMS options & encryption requirements — post-call recap

Hi Tim — thanks, these details are very helpful. Short answers below and next steps: 

1) In-transit: Redwood supports TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 for all API traffic. We recommend TLS 1.3 where possible.

2) At-rest: All primary data stores and backups use AES-256. For Hosted customers we encrypt using service-managed keys by default; for Dedicated/Private we offer full CMK via KMS integrations and HSM-backed options.

3) Customer-managed keys / HSM: We support BYOK workflows for major KMS providers (AWS KMS with CloudHSM, Google Cloud KMS with external key managers, Azure Key Vault with HSM). For Dedicated and Private deployments we can integrate HSM-backed key material so keys are non-exportable. Rotation policies can be applied; we support automated rotation schedules and manual rotation, quarterly rotation can be implemented.

4) Plaintext exposure: When using CMK with server-side encryption, Redwood does process request data in memory to serve inference; we have controls to minimize exposures (ephemeral memory, KV cache encryption, strict RBAC). If a no-plaintext guarantee is required, we can discuss client-side encryption (end-to-end) patterns or Private deployment models where customer-side decryption occurs in their network boundary. We will detail tradeoffs in the diagram.

5) Logs & retention: Default platform retention for logs is 90 days. We can support extended retention for audit logs up to 7 years in Dedicated/Private configurations; this affects storage costs. We can partition audit logs to limit PII in telemetry and provide redaction tooling where necessary.

Attachments: redwood-kms-options.pdf (detailed options + estimated pricing delta for HSM), acme-data-retention-qa.docx (mapping of retention ask to product capabilities).

Next steps (proposed):
- Vivek to run a 45-minute deep-dive next Tue/Wed with your security team to walk the key flow diagram and caching behavior.
- Rishi to produce rough cost delta for HSM-backed CMK per 100k requests/day.
- We’ll share SOC 2 bundle and architecture diagram before the deep-dive.

Are you available Tue Oct 26 at 10am ET for the technical deep-dive?

Best —
Marissa
